title: Your Policy Is Secretly a Harness: The Decision Geometry of Agent Interfaces
trick: Split an agent's return into the harness's optimal return (ceiling) and the policy's divergence from that optimum along its own paths (mismatch); a harness change moves both, training moves only mismatch.
framing_stripped: Called 'the decision geometry of agent interfaces' and 'your policy is secretly a harness'; it is the standard regularised-MDP performance-difference identity (Geist et al. 2019; O'Donoghue 2022) applied with the harness as the MDP, checked numerically in an exact-solve MiniWoB++ sandbox (three task families, one token per action, Qwen3.5-2B LoRA trained by exact policy gradient, optimum by soft Bellman dynamic programming), plus a teacher-as-optimum estimator run on three Terminal-Bench Lite tasks that orders five coding harnesses by a frozen Qwen3.5-9B's accuracy (sec. 2, 5.2, 6.3; App. F).
method_equations: Harness as interface $\mathcal{I}=(c_{\mathcal{I}},d_{\mathcal{I}},e_{\mathcal{I}})$: $c_{\mathcal{I}}$ encodes the semantic state $s$ into a prompt, $d_{\mathcal{I}}$ decodes a model output $y$ into a semantic action $a$ (an executed operation with its arguments), $e_{\mathcal{I}}$ executes it. The semantic policy of token policy $\pi_{\theta}$ is (eq. 1) $$\Pi_{\theta,\mathcal{I}}(a\mid s)=\sum_{y:\,d_{\mathcal{I}}(y;s)=a}\pi_{\theta}(y\mid c_{\mathcal{I}}(s)).$$ Regularised return (eq. 2), with $r_{\mathcal{I}}$ the reward including execution costs, $\pi^{\mathrm{ref}}_{\mathcal{I}}$ the reference (frozen base model read through the same interface), $\gamma$ the discount, $\tau$ the KL coefficient: $$J_{\mathcal{I}}(\Pi)=\mathbb{E}\Big[\sum_{t\ge 0}\gamma^{t}\big(r_{\mathcal{I}}(s_t,a_t)-\tau\log\tfrac{\Pi(a_t\mid s_t)}{\pi^{\mathrm{ref}}_{\mathcal{I}}(a_t\mid s_t)}\big)\Big].$$ Optimal action score (eq. 3), $Q^{*}_{\mathcal{I}}$ the soft-optimal action value: $$F^{*}_{\mathcal{I}}(s,a)=Q^{*}_{\mathcal{I}}(s,a)+\tau\log\pi^{\mathrm{ref}}_{\mathcal{I}}(a\mid s),\qquad \Pi^{*}_{\mathcal{I}}(\cdot\mid s)=\mathrm{softmax}(F^{*}_{\mathcal{I}}(s,\cdot)/\tau).$$ Behavioural identification (Prop. 3.1): an optimal checkpoint's log odds give score differences, $\tau\log\frac{\Pi(a\mid s)}{\Pi(b\mid s)}=F^{*}(s,a)-F^{*}(s,b)$; the readout of any checkpoint is its centred score $\widehat{F}_{\theta,\mathcal{I}}=\tau P_{\perp}\log\Pi_{\theta,\mathcal{I}}$ with $P_{\perp}=I-\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{\top}/n$, $n=|\mathcal{A}|$. Transfer split (eq. 5), interfaces 1 (training) and 2 (deployment), on aligned states: $$\widehat{F}_{\theta,2}-\bar{F}^{*}_{2}=\underbrace{\bar{F}^{*}_{1}-\bar{F}^{*}_{2}}_{g_{12}\ \text{target shift}}+\underbrace{\widehat{F}_{\theta,1}-\bar{F}^{*}_{1}}_{e_{1}\ \text{training residual}}+\underbrace{\widehat{F}_{\theta,2}-\widehat{F}_{\theta,1}}_{\eta_{12}\ \text{readout drift}}.$$ Performance gap (Prop. 5.1, eq. 6), $d^{\Pi}_{\mathcal{I}}$ the discounted state occupancy of $\Pi$: $$J_{\mathcal{I}}(\Pi^{*}_{\mathcal{I}})-J_{\mathcal{I}}(\Pi)=\frac{\tau}{1-\gamma}\,\mathbb{E}_{s\sim d^{\Pi}_{\mathcal{I}}}\mathrm{KL}\big(\Pi(\cdot\mid s)\,\|\,\Pi^{*}_{\mathcal{I}}(\cdot\mid s)\big).$$ Ceiling and mismatch (eq. 8): $C(\mathcal{I})=J_{\mathcal{I}}(\Pi^{*}_{\mathcal{I}})$, $M(\theta,\mathcal{I})$ the right-hand side of eq. 6 at $\Pi=\Pi_{\theta,\mathcal{I}}$, so $J_{\mathcal{I}}(\Pi_{\theta,\mathcal{I}})=C(\mathcal{I})-M(\theta,\mathcal{I})$ and for a frozen checkpoint (eq. 9) $J_2-J_1=(C_2-C_1)-(M_2-M_1)$. Adaptation threshold (Cor. 5.2, eq. 10): with $\theta_0$ the source checkpoint trained under $\mathcal{I}_1$ and $\theta_1$ its adaptation under $\mathcal{I}_2$, $J(\theta_1,\mathcal{I}_2)>J(\theta_0,\mathcal{I}_1)$ iff $$M(\theta_1,\mathcal{I}_2)<T,\qquad T=\Delta C+M(\theta_0,\mathcal{I}_1),\ \Delta C=C_2-C_1;$$ predicted gain $T-r_2$ with $r_2$ the mismatch of the checkpoint post-trained directly under $\mathcal{I}_2$ (sec. 5.3). Sampled estimator (eq. 11), $m$ states drawn from occupancy by stopping pilot rollouts at time $t$ with probability $(1-\gamma)\gamma^{t}$, $N$ actions sampled per state and smoothed to $\widetilde{p}(\cdot\mid s)=(n_a+\alpha)/(N+K\alpha)$ (eq. 29), $K$ the menu size: $$\widehat{M}=\frac{\tau}{(1-\gamma)m}\sum_{i=1}^{m}\mathrm{KL}\big(\widetilde{p}(\cdot\mid s_i)\,\|\,\Pi^{*}_{\mathcal{I}}(\cdot\mid s_i)\big).$$ Score-error bound (Prop. 6.1, eq. 12), $x_s=\widehat{F}_{\theta,\mathcal{I}}(s,\cdot)-\bar{F}^{*}_{\mathcal{I}}(s,\cdot)$, $\varepsilon_d^2=\mathbb{E}_{d}\|x_s\|_2^2$: $M(\theta,\mathcal{I})\le \varepsilon_d^2/(4\tau(1-\gamma))$. Coding-agent estimates (App. F.7, eqs. 31-32), $p_h$ and $q_h$ the student's and teacher's distributions over 13 action categories at the student's recorded states, $Y$ binary success, no discount, reference set to $p_h$ itself: $$\widetilde{C}_h=\mathbb{E}_{q_h}\Big[Y-\tau\sum_{t=0}^{L-1}\mathrm{KL}(q_h(\cdot\mid s_t)\,\|\,p_h(\cdot\mid s_t))\Big],\qquad \widetilde{M}_h=\frac{1}{4\tau}\,\mathbb{E}_{p_h}\Big[\sum_{t=0}^{L-1}\Big\|\tau P_{\perp}\log\frac{p_h(\cdot\mid s_t)}{q_h(\cdot\mid s_t)}\Big\|_2^2\Big],$$ with $\tau=0.1$; because the reference is $p_h$, the student's regularised return equals its success probability, so exact $C-M$ equals accuracy by construction and only the ordering of $\widetilde{C}_h-\widetilde{M}_h$ is tested.
load_bearing_assumption: That the harness induces a well-posed finite control problem whose semantic policy is what the model actually executes: every output decodes to one action in a finite menu with positive reference probability (eq. 1; App. B: 'Discarding unmodeled outputs changes the policy being measured'), and the KL-regularised optimum is the right notion of 'what the harness offers'. In MiniWoB++ this is engineered (one token per action, thinking disabled, temperature 1, ten decisions, $\gamma=0.95$, $\tau=0.1$). For coding agents it is replaced by 13 hand-made categories, a reference equal to the student's own distribution, and GPT-5.6-luna as the optimum; if the categories hide the decisions that carry success (which file, which command) or the teacher is far from optimal, $\widetilde{M}$ is a histogram distance to a stronger model and the five-harness ordering is a five-point coincidence.
weakest_component: The coding-agent study (sec. 6.3, App. F.7), which is the only result outside the toy sandbox and the one the abstract leads with: five harnesses, three probe tasks of 39, nine trajectories per harness per model (7 of 9 retained for some), Spearman $\rho=1.0$ over five points against $0.7$ and $-0.7$ for either term alone; accuracy spreads of $\pm 2.6$ to $\pm 7.8$ points over three runs overlap between adjacent harnesses (Terminus-2 $64.1\pm 5.1$ vs mini-SWE-agent $59.8\pm 7.8$), so the 'correct ordering' is of noisy means. $\widetilde{M}$ is a sum over decisions (eq. 32), so a harness that makes more model calls is penalised by count: DeepAgents has 14.2 decisions per trajectory against 4.9 for Terminus-2 and 'a mismatch per decision close to that of Terminus-2', yet the largest $\widetilde{M}$; mismatch alone already correlates $-0.7$ with accuracy, and the reference-equals-student choice makes exact $C-M$ equal accuracy by construction, so the test is only whether a teacher proxy preserves an ordering. Second: the mechanism results are a ten-decision finite graph with single-token menus trained by exact policy gradient on a 2B model, where the 85.0% to 19.2% field-reversal collapse is a model post-trained for 1,024 updates under one JSON layout; no frozen or frontier model's readout drift is reported under presentation variants (F.8 uses a frozen Qwen3.5-9B but only across H0-H5, not R1-R5).
regime: Sandbox: Qwen3.5-2B, LoRA rank 16, exact policy gradient (dynamic programming over compiled finite graphs), 1,024 updates x 4 tasks per harness, one RTX 4090 per run; three MiniWoB++ families (click-checkboxes, click-checkboxes-soft, ascending-numbers), horizon at most 10 decisions, $\gamma=0.95$, $\tau=0.1$, binary success reward, 1,440 train / 576 test tasks; six harnesses H0 (direct) to H5 (instructions only); H0 success 85.0%, presentation variants 19.2% to 86.0% (Table 1), adaptation gains in success $-2.5$ to $+12.6$ points over nine swaps (Table 10). Estimator calibration: $m=256$ occupancy states x $N=1024$ actions, 42,553.3 mean actor queries per task and condition (Table 11); 2.19 GPU-hours of new probability measurements (F.6). Coding: frozen Qwen3.5-9B, thinking on, temperature 0.6, 50 top-level decisions cap, five harnesses (DeepAgents, Pi coding-agent, DeepSeek Harness, Terminus-2, mini-SWE-agent), Terminal-Bench Lite 39 tasks, 3 runs, accuracy 47.9% to 64.1%; teacher GPT-5.6-luna; ceiling/mismatch probes on 3 tasks, 128 student and 64 teacher samples per recorded state, 13 action categories.
information_asymmetry: (1) Frozen comparison vs post-adaptation: what a harness offers (its ceiling $C$) is absent when harnesses are scored with a fixed checkpoint and present only after a solve (sandbox) or after further training under each candidate; the paper shows the frozen return change orders adaptation gains at Spearman $0.17$ while $T-r_2$ (ceiling gain plus the mismatch a directly-trained checkpoint keeps) orders them at $0.95$ (sec. 5.3, Table 10). For CL-W43-03 this settles that a fixed-model harness comparison is confounded by checkpoint-harness fit and names the two terms; it leaves open the claim's actual confounds, since reasoning effort and fresh restarts never appear as variables (decisions per trajectory is counted, never varied; no effort knob, no cost column), and the ceiling in deployment is itself a stronger model's success under the same harness, so 'harness ceiling' and 'what a stronger model does with this harness' are not separated. (2) Readout vs target: a presentation change moves only the model's expressed scores $\eta_{12}$ while the certified-optimal decision is unchanged; the trained 2B model changes its top action at 52.0% of states and falls from 85.0% to 19.2% success (Table 1), and 'the entire effect comes from the model's readout' (sec. 4.2). For CL-W43-10 this settles, at the extreme and with the optimum certified fixed, that form alone can dominate an agent's behaviour; it leaves open everything the claim's placebo arm needs: content is never varied (no same-length wrong-content block), the collapse is on a model post-trained under one layout rather than a frozen general model, and off-the-shelf models' readout drift under presentation variants is not reported. (3) Per-state vs per-harness: the student's and teacher's log odds at every recorded coding-agent state exist (128 and 64 samples each; App. F.7), which is a per-decision disagreement map, but only harness sums, decisions per trajectory and category shares are reported (Table 13, 14: 'the target inspects more often than the teacher' under all five harnesses). (4) Training vs deployment: the sandbox has full action distributions and a solved optimum; deployment has samples only, and the calibrated estimator costs 42,553 actor queries per task and condition on a ten-decision, roughly 30-action menu (Table 11), so the instrument that makes the identity usable has no cheap version yet. (5) Action vs category: the coding estimate exists at the level of 13 categories ('inspect', 'modify', 'plan', ...) while success depends on arguments the categories merge; the paper says so (F.7) and measures nothing below that level.
occupies: Published and not claimable: the identity $J=C-M$ (return equals harness ceiling minus occupancy-weighted KL mismatch) for a harness-induced KL-regularised control problem, the three-term split of transfer error (target shift, training residual, readout drift), the adaptation threshold $T=\Delta C+M(\theta_0,\mathcal{I}_1)$ and predictor $T-r_2$, the exact MiniWoB++ sandbox result that reversing observation-field order drops a post-trained Qwen3.5-2B from 85.0% to 19.2% success with the optimum certified unchanged, that all seven frozen-rejected swaps that raise the ceiling beat the source after adaptation (including three to an instructions-only harness that raises the ceiling through the reference), that sampled mismatch predicts return changes a hundredfold better than ceiling alone, and a teacher-as-optimum $\widetilde{C}-\widetilde{M}$ that orders five coding harnesses by Terminal-Bench Lite accuracy. For CL-W43-03 it occupies the sentence 'comparing harnesses with a fixed model mixes what each harness offers with how well that model uses it' and the ceiling/mismatch vocabulary; it does not occupy effort or restart as the confound, nor any cost-matched comparison. For CL-W43-10 it occupies 'a presentation change alone can make a trained agent fail on most tasks' as a certified-optimum result; it does not occupy a same-length wrong-content placebo, any content-versus-form comparison, or any frozen frontier model.

neighbors.title: Quantifying Language Models' Sensitivity to Spurious Features in Prompt Design or: How I learned to start worrying about prompt formatting
neighbors.trick: Sample many meaning-preserving prompt formats (FormatSpread) and report the spread of few-shot accuracy, up to 76 points on LLaMA-2-13B, with format rankings weakly correlated across models; this card's paper adds a control problem in which the optimal decision is certified unchanged, so the spread is attributed to readout drift alone.

neighbors.title: Harness-Zero: Harness Distillation via Agent-as-Harness
neighbors.trick: Let a harnessing agent, guided by a specialised harness, correct the student's responses in the target harness's action space and fine-tune on the corrected trajectories so the specialised harness can be removed at deployment (23.3% to 44.3% macro success); this card's paper says what such training can carry (the training harness's relative action scores) and that they are still expressed through whatever interface reads them.

neighbors.title: Co-Evolving Harnesses and Models: On-Policy Correction Helps Weaker Models Catch Up Where Imitation Fails
neighbors.trick: Evolve a harness around a weak model, find a stronger expert uses it better, show imitating the expert's full trajectories regresses 4 to 30 points on all seven tasks because it breaks model-harness fit, and instead have the expert rewrite only the failing turn of the weak model's own rollout; the 'fit' this breaks is this card's mismatch term.

neighbors.title: WHALE: A Simple Recipe for Joint Harness-Weight Optimization
neighbors.trick: Alternate rejection-sampling fine-tuning of the weights under the current harness with a Meta-Harness search for a better harness under the updated model, switching phases on fixed durations or a patience rule (Qwen3.5-2B/4B, 4.15-24.38 points over weight-only or harness-only); this card's paper gives the two terms such a loop moves and a threshold for when a harness switch pays.

neighbors.title: HarnessBandit: Joint Learnability-Transferability Scheduling for Multi-Harness Agentic Reinforcement Learning
neighbors.trick: Pick one harness per GRPO step by a bandit over learnability (mean absolute advantage) and transferability (cosine between gradient sketches across harnesses) to train Qwen3.5-2B across six harnesses; a multi-harness training recipe for the same harness-specific-preference problem this card's paper measures with a 6x6 checkpoint-by-harness geometry-error matrix.

theme_fit.why: scaffold sensitivity decomposed into what the harness offers and how well the checkpoint uses it, a presentation-only collapse (85.0% to 19.2%) with the optimum certified fixed, and a measured confound in every fixed-model harness leaderboard; the attribution question of the lane sentence

post-training dynamics appear (geometry error falls 69-90%, adaptation vs continuation branches) but as exact policy gradient on a ten-decision finite graph with a 2B model; no credit or long-horizon content
the readout term is sensitivity to how the context encodes the same state (field order, menu format, action codes); it is the harness's encoding, not a message the agent writes to itself

limitations_as_complaints: My coding-agent mismatch is a distance between histograms over 13 hand-made action categories, blind to which file or which command: 'The categories merge actions with different arguments and effects, so the estimates compare decisions at the level of these categories.' (App. F.7) — so the one real-harness result in the paper cannot say where in a trajectory a harness loses return.

I have no optimum outside the sandbox and only test an ordering: 'The estimates put a teacher that need not be optimal in place of the optimum, so $\widetilde{C}_{h}$ estimates a lower bound on the ceiling and $\widetilde{M}_{h}$ measures distance to the teacher.' (App. F.7) — five harnesses, three probe tasks of 39, nine trajectories each, Spearman 1.0 over five noisy means with overlapping run spreads (Table 2).

My calibrated mismatch estimator is not cheap: 'The selected budget uses about 119 times as many actor queries on calibration.' (App. F.5) — 42,553.3 mean actor queries per task and condition (Table 11) in a ten-decision, roughly 30-action sandbox, so the instrument that makes ceiling-minus-mismatch usable in deployment has no affordable version yet.
